title: Kobalos Linux Backdoor Investigation
description: Investigate a Kobalos Linux backdoor in a preconfigured sandbox environment.
outcomes: Identify the malicious process running on the target host
Detect communication between the target and C2 servers
Investigate data exfiltration from the target to next-target hosts

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Welcome to the Kobalos Linux Backdoor Investigation scenario. Your goal is to identify and investigate a Kobalos backdoor in our preconfigured sandbox environment.

levels.title: Access Target Host
levels.cloud_content: Connect to the target host using SSH with username 'cyrano' and password 'cyrano'.
levels.local_content: Access the local sandbox environment and connect to the target host using SSH with username 'cyrano' and password 'cyrano'.

levels.title: Identify Malicious Process
levels.content: List running processes on the target host and identify the malicious process.
levels.solution: Use the `ps` command to list running processes. Look for the sshd process that has been compromised by Kobalos.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.content: Check the output of the `ps` command for any unusual or unexpected processes.

hints.title: Hint 2
hints.content: Look for a process named 'sshd' that may have been compromised by Kobalos.

levels.title: Detect Communication with C2 Server
levels.content: Analyze network traffic to detect communication between the target host and the C2 server.
levels.solution: Use tools like `tcpdump` or `wireshark` to capture network traffic and look for connections between the target host and the IP address 151.80.57.191 on port 7070.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.content: Capture network traffic using tools like `tcpdump` or `wireshark` and look for connections to the C2 server.

hints.title: Hint 2
hints.content: Look for connections between the target host and IP address 151.80.57.191 on port 7070.

levels.title: Investigate Data Exfiltration
levels.content: Investigate data exfiltration from the target host to the next-target host.
levels.solution: Examine file transfer logs, SSH logs, or other relevant artifacts to identify potential data exfiltration between hosts. Look for the public key (id_ed25519.pub) that has been transferred from the target host to the next-target host.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.content: Examine file transfer logs, SSH logs, or other relevant artifacts for signs of data exfiltration between hosts.

hints.title: Hint 2
hints.content: Look for the public key (id_ed25519.pub) that has been transferred from the target host to the next-target host.
